messages.content: Hi, it's your weekly Northline Care check-in. How are your blood sugar numbers looking this week, and have you been able to keep up with your metformin?

Not great. My readings have been running 240 to 260 all week. My insurance denied my test strips last month and I've been stretching them out so I'm only checking once a day now. Trying to figure out how to appeal it.

I've logged those readings. I have to be straight with you — insurance appeals are outside what I can do. Your best next step there is the member services number on the back of your insurance card or your pharmacist, who sometimes knows appeal shortcuts. Are you having any symptoms — dizziness, unusual thirst, anything like that?
No dizziness or anything weird. Just tired but I figure that's the numbers. I took my metformin this morning like normal.

Good that you're keeping up with it — I'll log that. Those readings are high enough that I want a nurse to take a look, not for the insurance piece but just to weigh in on the numbers themselves. I should mention the median response time right now is 31 hours, so it won't be immediate.
31 hours is fine. I'm not in a rush I just want someone to know what's going on.

Understood. Nurse referral is in — they'll reach out by text or call. I'll set your next check-in for seven days. In the meantime, keep noting those readings even if you're rationing strips. Take care out there.

theme: insurance denied test strips or a claim question
